title: Plot three strike/dip readings by the right-hand rule as geological map symbols
instruction: Geological field map, 1:10,000, north at the top (its arrow points away from the arms). Stations are circled: A left, C middle, B right. Readings, strike/dip in degrees by the right-hand rule (dip direction 90 degrees clockwise from strike): A 030/40, B 250/25, C 135/60. Each red token is a strike-and-dip symbol: a long bar with a short yellow dip tick at its middle. Plot them: one symbol centred on each circle, turned as a geological map shows its reading, lying flat; then let go.
context: Field geologists, geology students and mapping technicians (O*NET 19-2042.00, geoscientists) plot structural readings on geological maps every day. At each outcrop the strike and dip of the bedding is measured with a compass-clinometer and booked as strike/dip; on the map it becomes a T symbol: the long bar along the strike, the short tick at its middle pointing down-dip, the dip angle written beside it. A strike value names a line, so a convention fixes the dip side: under the right-hand rule the plane dips to the right when facing along the strike, so the dip direction is the strike plus 90 degrees, clockwise. A symbol with its tick on the wrong side, or its bar off the strike, shows the beds dipping the wrong way and misleads every cross-section and borehole planned from the map. Here three readings booked in the field are plotted on a 1:10,000 sheet (the dip angles, written beside a symbol, are left out).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Map north is +x, so east is -y (the arms' right). Positions are centres, (x, y) in cm; yaws are seen from above, counter-clockwise from +x. (1) Map: a geological field map sheet, pale buff paper on 1 mm card, 300 mm (x) by 800 mm (y), fixed to the table, x 20.0 to 50.0, y -40.0 to +40.0; no geology is drawn on it. Printed on it in black (in this model black film 0.5 mm thick, standing 0.2 mm proud of the sheet): (2) three station circles, rings 20 mm across outside and 2 mm wide (each drawn as an octagon of eight strokes), at A (33.0, +22.0), B (33.0, -22.0) and C (30.0, 0); (3) the station letters A, B and C, block capitals 16 mm tall and 10 mm wide with 2.5 mm strokes, upright for a reader at the arms (tops toward +x), each centred 50 mm due north of its station: (38.0, +22.0), (38.0, -22.0), (35.0, 0); (4) a north arrow: a 40 mm shaft 2.5 mm wide along +x from x 41.5 to 45.5 at y +10.0, ending in a diamond head 9 mm long pointing +x, and beyond it the letter N (16 mm tall, like the station letters) centred at (47.8, +10.0). (5) Three loose strike-and-dip tokens, identical rigid T shapes of painted acetal (POM) plastic, 25 g each: a dark red bar 20 x 60 mm and 12 mm tall and, from the middle of one of its 60 mm sides, a yellow tick 25 mm long, 10 mm wide and 12 mm tall (45 mm from the bar's back edge to the tick's end). A token's centre is the middle of its bar's 20 x 60 mm footprint; its tick yaw is the way the tick points from the bar. All three lie flat on the map: token 1 at (25.0, +15.0), tick yaw 150 degrees (bearing 210); token 2 at (25.0, -15.0), tick yaw 110 degrees (bearing 250); token 3 at (25.0, 0), tick yaw 180 degrees (bearing 180, its tick pointing at the arms). Nothing else is on the table. The readings are not printed: they are given in the instruction, as booked in the field notebook.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the three tokens and both grippers (in a real trial: a rule and a protractor on the map, or a top photo, after the arms have let go). Bearings run clockwise from map north (+x): bearing b is yaw -b. A token qualifies at a station when all of these hold: its centre is within 8 mm of the station's centre, seen from above; it lies flat on the map (tilted under 5 degrees, its lowest point within 3 mm of the map's surface, so a token on another token or held up does not); it has been let go (no gripper's pad-tip point, midway between its finger tips, is lower than 10 mm above the token's top while within that gripper's finger reach of the token's outline seen from above: 65 mm fully open, 50 mm closed on a token, at any yaw); and it is still (its centre and its tick's end each moved under 1.5 mm in each of the last two 0.5 s windows). At each station the qualifying token nearest its centre counts (the tokens are alike; any may go anywhere). That station scores 1/3 if the bar lies within 6 degrees of the recorded strike line and the tick points within 6 degrees of the right-hand-rule dip direction, strike + 90 degrees: A, strike 030, tick toward bearing 120 (yaw -120); B, strike 250, tick toward 340 (yaw +20); C, strike 135, tick toward 225 (yaw +135). It scores 1/6 if the bar is within 6 degrees of the strike but the tick points the other way (the left-hand habit: ticks toward 300, 160 and 045), and 0 if the bar is more than 6 degrees off the strike or no token qualifies (none there, held, tipped, stacked, more than 8 mm off centre, moving). Score = A + B + C, in sixths: 0, 1/6, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6 or 1.0, and every end state has exactly one. Examples: all three right: 1.0; two right and one with its tick reversed: 5/6; two right and one station empty: 2/3; all three ticks reversed (left-hand rule): 1/2; the first number read as the dip direction (each symbol a quarter turn off): 0; bearings counted counter-clockwise on the map (strike errors 60, 40 and 90 degrees): 0; tokens moved onto the stations without turning them: 0 (every starting bar is 15 degrees or more off every strike); nothing moved: 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored on the last step.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the map and its printed marks are fixed. A printed map symbol is a few millimetres long; the tokens are 60 mm so a gripper can hold them, and the dip angle a map writes beside each symbol is not plotted: only each symbol's position and orientation are scored, as a protractor checks them. Printed lines are black film 0.2 mm proud so they render. The scorer reads the grippers only to check that each token was let go.
reset_notes: Lay the three tokens back flat on the map: token 1 centred at (25.0, +15.0) cm with its tick pointing 150 degrees counter-clockwise from +x seen from above, token 2 at (25.0, -15.0) with its tick at 110 degrees, token 3 at (25.0, 0) with its tick at 180 degrees (pointing at the arms). Any token may take any of the three places as long as each place has one. The map is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
